sources.entry: tornado - A web framework and asynchronous networking library.

summary.one_liner: Tornado is a Python web framework and asynchronous networking library that uses non-blocking network I/O to handle large numbers of open connections.
summary.what_it_does: Tornado provides a Python web framework built around request handler classes and an Application object that maps URL patterns to handlers. It uses non-blocking network I/O so it can keep tens of thousands of connections open at once. The README names long polling and WebSockets as suited use cases for long-lived per-user connections. The README's example shows a minimal "Hello, world" app that listens on a port and runs under asyncio. It also links to a simple chat room example that uses asynchronous features. Full documentation is referenced externally, and the README excerpt does not list further features.
use_cases: applications needing many long-lived user connections
how_to_run: Save the Hello, world example as a Python file
Run the file with python to start the server on port 8888
notable: Non-blocking network I/O allowing tens of thousands of open connections
Built-in web framework with RequestHandler and Application classes
Native WebSocket and long polling support
caveats: README excerpt provides little detail on installation requirements or platform limits
Full documentation is referenced externally rather than included in the README
